# Igor B. Martins

> Igor B. Martins is an economic historian at Lund University researching inequality, slavery, wealth, labour markets, and economic resilience in Africa.

This site presents the research, publications, projects, and teaching of Igor B. Martins. His work examines how ownership, labour markets, access to finance, and political power shape inequality and influence how people and countries withstand economic disruption.

## Research areas

- African economic history and long-term inequality
- Slavery, emancipation, wealth, and labour coercion in the Cape Colony
- Labour markets, prices, incomes, and living standards in Ghana
- Climate exposure, asset ownership, and inequality
- Economic shrinking, resilience, and long-run development
- International scientific cooperation, research policy, and geopolitics

- [Research and publications](https://ibmartins.com/research.llms.md): Published work, manuscripts under review, current research, essays, and media.
- [Research projects](https://ibmartins.com/projects.llms.md): Funded work on inequality, colonial political economy, labour, climate, and economic resilience.
- [Biography](https://ibmartins.com/about.llms.md): Research agenda, academic background, affiliations, and contact information.
- [Teaching and supervision](https://ibmartins.com/teaching.llms.md): Current and previous teaching, student supervision, and teaching recognition.
- [Curriculum vitae](https://ibmartins.com/files/igor-b-martins-cv.pdf): Complete academic CV in PDF format.
